en.askTitle: Swap in your own dates, income and insurance and get the same DTV-versus-LTR comparison before you commit to Thailand
en.runTitle: Berlin to Chiang Mai: a German freelance designer choosing between two Thai long-stay visas

en.template: I’m a German freelance {profession} planning Chiang Mai from {arrival} to {departure}, possibly through {later}. My €{amount} is {incomeType}, savings history is {savings}, clients/IP arrangements are {clients}, German home/business access is {home}, and insurance is {insurance}. Help me organise a DTV document timeline, separate calendar-year day counts and the questions for my German–Thai tax adviser and insurer.

phases.title: Read Thai visa and tax rules and German residency and insurance rules from official sources
phases.note: Thai visa and tax rules on one side, German residency, treaty and health insurance on the other
phases.judgment: It would not let a client’s location decide where income is taxed: design work done in Chiang Mai is ordinarily Thai-source income even for EU clients. And where it could not retrieve the official Germany–Thailand treaty, it marked those points “unconfirmed pending official reread”.

phases.title: Write the guide, with the comparison table, cost table and a source list
phases.note: Recommendation first, then costs in THB and EUR with the arithmetic shown

phases.title: Independent check of every claim and number, plus desktop and phone layout tests
phases.judgment: An independent colleague checked 47 claims; all 31 money figures and date calculations passed. It also flagged an inconsistent wording about subsidiary ownership on the Thai investment board’s page, rather than letting it through.

workers: Read Thailand’s tax rules for a freelancer living in Chiang Mai, including the Long-Term Resident visa and tax-treaty provisions

Read the finished guide against its source list, recomputed every money figure and rule claim on their own
